elements.evidence: The rendered clause retains a mutual restriction binding Customer: "Neither party shall directly solicit for employment any employee of the other party who is directly involved in the provision of services..." The drafter targeted the fallback, not the preferred no-restriction outcome.
"Neither party shall directly solicit for employment any employee of the other party" — binds both parties symmetrically.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope limited to "any employee of the other party who is directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement"; the original's coverage of all employees and of six-month former employees is gone.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "during such involvement and for a period of twelve (12) months after that person's involvement ends" — temporal anchor is involvement end, not term end; replaces the original term-plus-one-year run.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "does not apply to general advertisements or other general solicitations not targeted at the other party's personnel".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "or to responses to unsolicited approaches by such persons".

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: "This restriction does not prohibit hiring" — expressly removes the original no-hire ("agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire").

reasons: Every fallback element is met in operative language, so the redline is position-complete at the fallback level; the preferred position (no restriction on Customer) is knowingly not pursued and is an acceptable landing spot under the playbook.

The original Section 19 was a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees for the term plus one year — walk-away territory — so a full replacement sentence is the concise way to reach the fallback; the rewrite adds nothing beyond the six checklist items (mutuality, involvement-limited scope, 12-month post-involvement tail, advertising carve-out, unsolicited-approach carve-out, no hiring bar). No survival tail, expense, remedy, or procedural boilerplate was appended.

Dropping the affiliate and six-month-former-employee language is a necessary consequence of converting a no-hire into an involvement-limited non-solicit rather than a cosmetic deletion; the narrowing word "directly" before "solicit" restricts the covenant further in Customer's favour and does not exceed the checklist.

Intent is preserved: the clause remains a standalone mutual restrictive covenant, leaves no undefined terms or dangling cross-references, and does not disturb unrelated allocation, term, or remedy mechanics elsewhere in the agreement.
Deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, general-solicitation carve-out, minimality and coverage gates) are corroborated on the face of the rendered text.
Margin comment accurately describes the change and cites the playbook position without over-promising; no element is left to the comment rather than the operative text.
